description:
`test` and `[` over long operand lists, runs of `!` and nested parentheses, with bash's syntax
errors; runs of `!` in `[[ ]]`. Lists and runs are read in loops, however long; only parentheses
nest, up to a limit.

Each case name starts with `test operands: `.

cases.name: test operands: 5000 operands joined by -a
cases.script:
test x $(printf -- '-a x %.0s' {1..5000}); echo rc=$?; [ x $(printf -- '-a x %.0s' {1..5000}) ]; echo rc=$?
test x $(printf -- '-a x %.0s' {1..5000}) -a ''; echo rc=$?

cases.name: test operands: 5000 empty operands joined by -o
cases.script: a=(); for i in $(seq 5000); do a+=('' -o); done; test "${a[@]}" ''; echo rc=$?; a+=(x); test "${a[@]}"; echo rc=$?

cases.name: test operands: a run of 2000 ! before an operand
cases.script:
test $(printf '%.0s! ' {1..2000}) x; echo rc=$?; test $(printf '%.0s! ' {1..2001}) x; echo rc=$?
[ $(printf '%.0s! ' {1..2001}) -n '' -a x ]; echo rc=$?

cases.name: test operands: -f over 8000 files joined by -a and -o
cases.script:
mkdir /tmp/many && cd /tmp/many && touch $(seq -f f%g 8000)
a=($(printf -- '-f f%s -a ' $(seq 8000)) -f f1); test "${a[@]}"; echo rc=$?
a=($(printf -- '-f g%s -o ' $(seq 8000)) -f f1); [ "${a[@]}" ]; echo rc=$?
a=($(printf -- '-f f%s -a ' $(seq 8000)) -f nope); test "${a[@]}"; echo rc=$?

cases.name: test operands: every operand of -a and -o is evaluated
cases.script: test 1 -eq 1 -o x -eq 1; echo rc=$?; test 1 -eq 2 -a x -eq 1; echo rc=$?; test x -eq 1 -o 1 -eq 1; echo rc=$?

cases.name: test operands: syntax errors are worded as bash words them
test operands: parentheses nested deeper are refused

stderr.text:
bash: line 1: test: maximum nesting level exceeded: deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool
bash: line 2: [: maximum nesting level exceeded: deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: test reads and evaluates each level of parentheses recursively, so it refuses more than 64 (README, Limits); bash reads 2,000

cases.name: test operands: a run of 3000 ! in [[ ]]
